questions.question: Which EC2 pricing model allows you to commit to a specific dollar amount per hour rather than a specific instance type?

explanation.correct: Savings Plans commit you to a $/hour spend amount, not a specific instance type or configuration.
explanation.why: A (Reserved) locks you to a specific instance type and region. C (Spot) has no commitment. D (Dedicated Host) is about physical isolation.

questions.question: What is the maximum discount you can receive with Spot Instances compared to On-Demand pricing?

explanation.correct: Spot Instances can offer up to 90% discount compared to On-Demand prices.
explanation.why: 72% is the discount for Reserved Instances and some Savings Plans. Spot Instances offer the highest possible discount because you're using spare capacity.

questions.question: How much advance warning does AWS give before terminating a Spot Instance?

explanation.correct: AWS sends a 2-minute interruption notice before terminating a Spot Instance.
explanation.why: This 2-minute window allows your application to checkpoint work, save state, or gracefully shut down before the instance is reclaimed.

questions.question: Which EC2 pricing model is BEST for a company running Oracle Database with per-physical-core licensing?

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts give you visibility into physical core and socket topology, which is required for BYOL (Bring Your Own License) software like Oracle.
explanation.why: On-Demand and Reserved share hardware with other customers and don't expose physical topology. Spot is not appropriate for databases. Dedicated Hosts are the only option for per-core BYOL licensing.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a Dedicated Host and a Dedicated Instance?

options.text: Dedicated Hosts are cheaper than Dedicated Instances
Dedicated Hosts give you a full physical server with core/socket visibility; Dedicated Instances only isolate at account level
Dedicated Instances support BYOL; Dedicated Hosts do not

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts = full physical server dedicated to you + visible physical topology + BYOL support. Dedicated Instances = hardware isolated to your account but no physical visibility and limited BYOL.
explanation.why: BYOL and physical core/socket visibility are only available with Dedicated Hosts, not Dedicated Instances.

questions.question: Which type of Savings Plan covers EC2, AWS Lambda, AND AWS Fargate under a single commitment?

explanation.correct: Compute Savings Plans are the most flexible type and cover EC2, Lambda, and Fargate automatically.
explanation.why: EC2 Instance Savings Plans only cover EC2 within a specific instance family and region. SageMaker is for ML workloads only.

questions.question: Which Savings Plan type offers the DEEPEST discount at up to 72%?

explanation.correct: EC2 Instance Savings Plans offer up to 72% because you commit to a specific instance family and region, trading flexibility for a deeper discount.
explanation.why: Compute Savings Plans offer up to 66% because they are more flexible. Greater flexibility = lower maximum discount.

questions.question: A company wants to process large video encoding jobs that take 3 hours each. Jobs can be stopped and restarted if needed. Which pricing model gives the best cost savings?

explanation.correct: Spot Instances are perfect for fault-tolerant, restartable batch jobs. The 90% discount makes them the cheapest option.
explanation.why: On-Demand has no discount. Reserved requires a 1-3 year commitment and is best for steady usage. Dedicated Hosts are for BYOL and physical isolation needs.

questions.question: What does BYOL stand for in the context of Dedicated Hosts?

explanation.correct: BYOL means Bring Your Own License — using software licenses you already own (like Oracle or Windows Server) on AWS infrastructure instead of paying AWS for licensing.
explanation.why: BYOL is a key use case for Dedicated Hosts because enterprise licenses are often tied to physical hardware topology.

questions.question: Which payment option for Savings Plans gives you the HIGHEST discount?

explanation.correct: All Upfront gives the highest discount because AWS receives guaranteed full payment immediately, reducing their financial risk.
explanation.why: No Upfront gives the lowest discount among commitment options. Monthly On-Demand is not a Savings Plans option.

questions.question: Which Spot Instance interruption behavior saves the RAM state to EBS so the instance can resume exactly where it left off?

explanation.correct: Hibernate saves the RAM state to the root EBS volume. When the instance restarts, RAM is reloaded and applications continue where they left off.
explanation.why: Terminate deletes the instance. Stop preserves storage but not RAM state. Pause is not a valid EC2 interruption behavior.

questions.question: What is the minimum requirement for using Hibernate as a Spot interruption behavior?

options.text: Instance must have at least 32GB RAM
Root EBS volume must be encrypted
Instance must be in a private subnet

explanation.correct: Hibernate requires an encrypted root EBS volume because the RAM contents (which may contain sensitive data) are written to disk.
explanation.why: This is a security requirement — RAM data written to disk must be encrypted.

questions.question: A Spot Fleet is configured to use t3.medium instances in us-east-1a only. What is the main risk with this configuration?

options.text: The fleet will be too expensive
Low resilience — if that AZ has no spare capacity, the fleet cannot launch instances
Spot Fleets cannot use t3.medium instances
The fleet will automatically use Dedicated Hosts

explanation.correct: Using a single instance type in a single AZ limits the Spot Fleet's ability to get capacity. Best practice is to diversify across multiple instance types and multiple AZs.
explanation.why: Spot Fleet's power comes from diversification — if one pool is unavailable or expensive, it uses another.

questions.question: A company has been running 20 t3.large On-Demand instances for 8 months and expects to continue for at least 2 more years. What would you recommend to maximize savings?

options.text: Migrate to Spot Instances to save 90%
Purchase a 3-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the t3 family with All Upfront payment
Keep On-Demand and wait for pricing to drop
Use Dedicated Hosts for bulk discounts

explanation.correct: A 3-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan with All Upfront provides the maximum discount (up to 72%) for predictable, steady long-term workloads.
explanation.why: Spot would risk interruptions for production servers. On-Demand has no discount. Dedicated Hosts don't provide bulk discounts for regular instances.

questions.question: You check Spot pricing history and see that t3.micro prices in us-east-1a have been very stable and low for months. What does this suggest?

options.text: AWS is about to increase Spot prices dramatically
There is consistently high spare capacity for t3.micro in that AZ — low interruption risk
The instance type is being discontinued
This instance type does not support Spot pricing

explanation.correct: Stable low Spot prices indicate consistent surplus capacity in that pool. Low prices = low demand for that capacity = lower interruption risk.
explanation.why: You can also check the EC2 Spot Instance Advisor for official interruption frequency data before selecting an instance type.

questions.question: Which of the following workloads is MOST appropriate for Spot Instances?

options.text: Nightly log analysis batch job with checkpointing enabled

explanation.correct: Batch jobs with checkpointing can resume after interruption without data loss — this is the ideal Spot use case.
explanation.why: Production web servers, databases, and payment processing cannot tolerate unexpected interruptions. Checkpointed batch jobs can.

questions.question: What is the term used for a Savings Plan where you commit to a specific instance family in a specific region?

explanation.correct: EC2 Instance Savings Plans commit you to a specific instance family (e.g., t3) in a specific region (e.g., us-east-1) for the deepest EC2 discount.
explanation.why: Compute Savings Plans are not locked to an instance family or region — they apply more broadly.

questions.question: A team submits a Spot request but no capacity is available at the current Spot price. What is the status of the request?

explanation.correct: When capacity is unavailable at the requested price, the Spot request enters 'open' state and waits until capacity becomes available or the request expires.
explanation.why: 'open' means the request is waiting. 'fulfilled' means an instance was launched. 'cancelled' means you manually cancelled it.

questions.question: A financial services company must ensure their workloads run on hardware not shared with any other organization due to regulatory requirements. Which option should they choose?

options.text: Default tenancy EC2 with VPC isolation

explanation.correct: Dedicated Instances guarantee that your EC2 instances run on hardware dedicated to your AWS account, satisfying basic physical isolation compliance requirements.
explanation.why: If they also needed BYOL support or placement control, Dedicated Hosts would be the answer. For basic isolation compliance, Dedicated Instances suffice.

questions.question: What tool does AWS provide to help determine the optimal Savings Plan commitment amount based on historical usage?

options.text: AWS Savings Plans Recommendations in the console / Cost Explorer

explanation.correct: AWS Savings Plans Recommendations (accessible via the EC2 Savings Plans console or AWS Cost Explorer) analyzes your past usage to recommend the optimal commitment amount.
explanation.why: AWS Config monitors configuration changes. CloudWatch monitors performance metrics. Trusted Advisor does provide some cost recommendations but the Savings Plans console and Cost Explorer give the most detailed Savings Plans analysis.

questions.question: A company uses EC2 Instance Savings Plans for their t3 family in us-east-1. They decide to upgrade to t4g instances (Graviton2). What happens to their Savings Plan?

options.text: The Savings Plan automatically covers the t4g instances
The Savings Plan does not apply — they would need a new plan for the t4g family
The Savings Plan covers any instance in us-east-1 regardless of family
The old plan must be cancelled before purchasing a new one

explanation.correct: EC2 Instance Savings Plans are locked to a specific instance family (t3 in this case). Switching to t4g (a different family) means the existing plan no longer applies to those instances.
explanation.why: This is a key limitation of EC2 Instance Savings Plans vs Compute Savings Plans. A Compute Savings Plan would have covered the t4g instances automatically.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Spot Fleet is TRUE?

options.text: Spot Fleet can only use a single instance type
Spot Fleet can combine Spot and On-Demand instances to meet target capacity
Spot Fleet automatically converts to Reserved Instances when capacity is low
Spot Fleet is only available in specific AWS regions

explanation.correct: Spot Fleet can be configured to use a mix of Spot Instances and On-Demand Instances. On-Demand acts as a fallback to ensure minimum capacity even when Spot capacity is unavailable.
explanation.why: This hybrid approach gives you cost savings through Spot while maintaining capacity reliability through On-Demand.

questions.question: From an AWS billing perspective, how are Dedicated Hosts priced differently from regular EC2 instances?

options.text: Dedicated Hosts are billed per virtual CPU used
Dedicated Hosts are billed per physical host per hour, regardless of how many instances run on it
Dedicated Hosts are billed the same as On-Demand instances
Dedicated Hosts are only billed when instances are running on them

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts are billed per physical host per hour. You pay for the entire host whether you run 1 instance or fill it with many instances.
explanation.why: This billing model means Dedicated Hosts are cost-effective only when you fully utilize the host capacity. An empty Dedicated Host still incurs hourly charges.

questions.question: A company wants to maximize cost savings on EC2 while also running some workloads on AWS Fargate containers and AWS Lambda functions. A single commitment should cover all three. What should they purchase?

options.text: Separate Reserved Instances for EC2 and separate Reserved Concurrency for Lambda
EC2 Instance Savings Plan + separate Lambda Provisioned Concurrency

explanation.correct: Compute Savings Plans automatically apply discounts across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda under a single per-hour commitment — the most flexible and comprehensive option.
explanation.why: EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not cover Lambda or Fargate. There's no such thing as a 'Reserved Concurrency' plan. SageMaker Savings Plans are for ML workloads only.

questions.question: A data science team runs training jobs that each take 6–12 hours. The jobs use checkpointing every 30 minutes. What Spot configuration provides the best combination of cost savings and resilience?

options.text: Single Spot Instance in us-east-1a with t3.xlarge
Spot Fleet across multiple instance types and multiple AZs with Stop interruption behavior
Spot Fleet with Terminate behavior and no checkpointing
On-Demand instances — Spot is too risky for 6-12 hour jobs

explanation.correct: A Spot Fleet diversified across multiple instance types and AZs reduces the chance of simultaneous interruption. Stop behavior preserves the EBS volume so the job can resume from the last checkpoint after re-launch.
explanation.why: A single instance in one AZ has higher interruption risk. Checkpointing every 30 minutes means at most 30 minutes of rework — acceptable. On-Demand would miss the 90% savings.

questions.question: An architect notices that a company's Savings Plan is applying 100% to their t3 instances but they've launched new c5 instances that aren't receiving any discount. Their Savings Plan is an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the t3 family. What should they do?

options.text: Cancel the existing Savings Plan and repurchase for c5
Purchase an additional Savings Plan — either EC2 Instance SP for c5 family, or upgrade to Compute SP for broader coverage
Move the c5 instances to the us-east-1 region to get the discount
Reserved Instances for the c5 family will override and provide coverage

explanation.correct: You cannot cancel a Savings Plan once purchased. The correct approach is to purchase an additional plan. A Compute Savings Plan would cover both t3 and c5 plus any future instance families.
explanation.why: EC2 Instance SPs are family-locked. You need a separate plan for each family, OR switch to a Compute SP for flexibility. Savings Plans cannot be cancelled — they run for the full term.

questions.question: Which AWS service should you use BEFORE purchasing a Savings Plan to analyze potential savings based on actual usage history?

options.text: AWS Cost Explorer with Savings Plans recommendations

explanation.correct: AWS Cost Explorer provides Savings Plans recommendations based on your actual EC2 usage history, showing you exactly how much you'd save with different commitment amounts.
explanation.why: CloudTrail logs API calls. Config tracks configuration changes. Systems Manager manages operational tasks. Cost Explorer is the cost optimization and analysis tool.

questions.question: A company running Spot Instances for ML training needs to ensure that if an interruption occurs, the training job resumes from the last epoch checkpoint (not from scratch). The training framework writes checkpoints to disk. Which interruption behavior should they configure?

options.text: Terminate with a separate EBS volume attached for checkpoints
None — Spot Instances cannot reliably support ML training

explanation.correct: Terminate with checkpoints on a separate (non-root) EBS volume is the most reliable approach. The separate EBS volume persists even when the root volume is deleted. The training framework reads the checkpoint on next launch and resumes.
explanation.why: Hibernate also works but requires encrypted EBS and is limited to specific instance types and sizes. Stop is another option but Terminate with separate EBS is the standard ML training pattern. Stop preserves the root volume too.

questions.question: Under Dedicated Host billing, what happens if you run zero instances on your Dedicated Host for an entire day?

options.text: No charge — you are only billed when instances run
Full hourly charges apply for the entire day — the host is allocated to you
AWS automatically releases the host and stops billing

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts are billed per host per hour regardless of instance utilization. You pay for the physical server allocation, not for running instances on it.
explanation.why: This is why Dedicated Hosts require careful capacity planning — unused host capacity still costs money. Always try to fill hosts with as many instances as possible.

questions.question: A Solutions Architect is designing a cost strategy for a company's mixed workload: 60% steady-state web servers, 30% variable batch processing, 10% Oracle Database servers that require BYOL licensing. What is the MOST cost-effective combination?

options.text: All Reserved Instances with full upfront payment
Savings Plans for web servers + Spot Instances for batch processing + Dedicated Hosts for Oracle
Spot Instances for everything + Dedicated Instances for Oracle

explanation.correct: This is the optimal mixed strategy: Savings Plans for steady web servers (flexibility + up to 72% discount), Spot for batch (up to 90% discount + fault-tolerant), Dedicated Hosts for Oracle BYOL (physical core visibility for licensing compliance).
explanation.why: All On-Demand misses all discounts. All Reserved is inflexible. Spot for web servers risks availability. Dedicated Instances for Oracle don't support full BYOL with per-core licensing.
